about: Tourism in Calgary: the figures Calgary's own tourism bodies publish, what makes Calgary different, what other destinations did to grow (with their results), and the incentives in use. Checked by hand in November 2026 from the sources given with each item; figures are as the source states them, with its date. Statistics Canada's arrivals and airport figures are in tourism.json (get_dashboard section tourism). Facts, not recommendations: the report draws its own options from them.

calgary_2025.goal: Double visitor spending to $6 billion by 2035 (about 6% a year)
calgary_2025.q1_2026: International visitor spending up 15.6% and international passengers at YYC up 9.6% on Q1 2025

airport.connecting_note: More than seven million international travellers connect through Calgary each year without leaving the airport (Tourism Calgary, June 2026).
airport.us_arrivals_april_2025: US arrivals at YYC up 29% on April 2024 while US arrivals at Canada's major airports fell 6% (CBC, June 2025)

sources.title: Tourism Calgary and WestJet launch Calgary Stopover Program
Calgary 'bucking the trend' as U.S. visits surge

calgary_stopover_program.what: A pilot: travellers on WestJet's London Heathrow and Edinburgh routes add a Calgary stay of up to seven days at no extra airfare, with 19 hotel offers and the Calgary Attractions Pass; more routes and markets planned.

source.title: Tourism Calgary and WestJet launch Calgary Stopover Program

banff_gateway.note: A record; Parks Canada counts April to March. The park manages crowding with shuttles to Lake Louise and Moraine Lake, Roam transit and paid parking pilots. Most visitors who fly in land at YYC, about 130 km away.

source.title: Banff National Park sets new record with 4.5 million visitors (citing CBC)
Calgary Stampede economic impact report shows 33 per cent jump in 6 years

levies.destination_marketing_fee: Up to 6% of room revenue, charged by about 60 Calgary Hotel Association hotels; voluntary for guests today.
levies.from_2027: The Traveller Protection and Destination Development Act takes full effect 1 January 2027: the full price including the destination marketing fee shown at booking, the fee held by a third-party trustee, one approved fee and one destination marketing organization per community.
levies.short_term_rentals: The 6% levy applies; platforms collect it; hosts need a City business licence.

source.title: Hotel and lodging tax in Calgary 2026
source.publisher: RoomMaster (secondary source; check the Act and Alberta's levy page)

rail.status_june_2026: Alberta's passenger rail master plan puts airport links for Calgary and Edmonton (LRT extensions) first, with $15 million over three years for planning; Calgary to Banff and Edmonton to Calgary high-speed rail are targets within about 30 years; full build-out at least $60 billion. A private proposal (Liricon Capital) for Calgary to Banff beside the CPKC line was not preferred in the plan.

source.title: Alberta advances plans for passenger rail lines throughout the province

indigenous_tourism.mou: Tourism Calgary and Indigenous Tourism Alberta signed an MOU on 23 January 2025: $1 million over four years (with the Calgary Hotel Association) to develop and promote Indigenous experiences, and Tourism Calgary pays membership dues for Treaty 7 and Metis District businesses.
indigenous_tourism.demand: One in three international visitors seek an authentic Indigenous experience; two in three meetings, conventions and major events coming to Calgary want one.
indigenous_tourism.glenbow: Glenbow reopens (2026 to 2027) as the JR Shaw Centre for Arts & Culture with permanent free admission (a $25 million endowment), a Blackfoot Gallery curated with Elders from four Blackfoot Nations, eight floors and 325,000 sq ft.

sources.title: Indigenous Tourism Alberta and Tourism Calgary sign MOU

uniqueness.what: Banff (about 130 km, 1.5 hours) had a record 4.5 million visitors in 2025-26; Calgary is the nearest international airport. No other Canadian city of a million people is this close to a world-famous mountain park.
Mountains, lakes, badlands, dinosaurs, Blackfoot heritage and five UNESCO World Heritage Sites within a few hours, from one city with an international airport (around_calgary).
uniqueness.source: Drive times from OpenStreetMap routing; UNESCO list via AFAR

uniqueness.what: Since 1912; $721 million economic impact across Alberta in 2025, a western heritage brand known worldwide.
Host of the 1988 Winter Olympics; WinSport (Canada Olympic Park) and the Olympic Oval still run sport, training and events.

One of Canada's sunniest large cities, with chinook winds that break winter cold. The popular '333 days of sunshine' claim has no published source; use Environment and Climate Change Canada's sunshine hours instead.
uniqueness.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada climate normals; University of Calgary student blog (April 2026) for the popular claim

uniqueness.what: Blackfoot Confederacy, Tsuut'ina and Stoney Nakoda Nations and Metis Region 3; Blackfoot Crossing (about 1.5 hours), the new Blackfoot Gallery at Glenbow, and an Indigenous tourism MOU.
The Royal Tyrrell Museum and the badlands of Drumheller are a day trip (about 1.5 hours).
uniqueness.source: General knowledge; check the museum site

uniqueness.what: Glenbow will be the first major Canadian museum with permanently free admission; Studio Bell (National Music Centre), the Central Library, Heritage Park and the Calgary Zoo.
Ranked 5th in the EIU Global Liveability Index 2024 and 18th in 2025 (the drop from healthcare scores).
110 non-stop destinations; WestJet's hub; new non-stops to Sao Paulo and Abu Dhabi in 2026.

lessons_from_other_destinations.what: A free stopover of up to seven days on transatlantic tickets turned a connection point into a destination; Iceland's visitors roughly tripled from 2010 to 2016, with Icelandair's marketing a major driver. Later, crowding and pressure on housing became issues.
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: The closest model to the Calgary Stopover pilot (WestJet as the hub airline, YYC as the connection point).

lessons_from_other_destinations.what: Since 1987, transit passengers with 5.5 to 24 hours between flights get a free 2.5-hour city tour (Changi Airport, Singapore Airlines and the tourism board); over 80,000 took it in 2019, when transit passengers were about 30% of Changi's traffic.
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: A short free tour (downtown, the river, the Peace Bridge, or a mountain-view drive) for long connections at YYC.

lessons_from_other_destinations.what: 19.59 million international overnight visitors in 2025, a third record year, hotel occupancy 80.7% across 154,000 rooms; credited to a city economic plan (D33), year-round festivals (Shopping Festival, Summer Surprises, Fitness Challenge), visa policy, and marketing partnerships with hotel and payment brands.
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: Signature festivals in the slow months, and partnerships with airlines, hotels and card brands.

sources.title: Dubai tourism hits record 19.59m visitors in 2025

lessons_from_other_destinations.place: Airline stopovers (Qatar, Emirates, Etihad, Turkish, TAP, Copa)
lessons_from_other_destinations.what: Hub airlines turn connections into stays: TAP free stopovers up to 10 days; Qatar discounted hotel packages for 12 to 96 hours; Emirates free hotel for 8 to 26 hour connections; Etihad and Turkish free hotel nights; Copa free 24-hour to 7-day stopovers.
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: Calgary's stopover could add hotel or attraction value, not only free airfare, and extend beyond UK routes.

lessons_from_other_destinations.what: 65 million visitors in 2025 (52.4 million domestic, 12.5 million international, down 3.2%), $84.7 billion economic impact, 397,000 jobs, hotel occupancy 84.2%; 1,515 meetings and events booked; the World Cup 2026 expected to bring 1.2 million visitors.
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: Conventions and major events as a steady base; a city of Calgary's size can win events in their category.

lessons_from_other_destinations.what: 37.6 million visitors and $10.5 billion in 2025; 42% of overnight visitors arrive by air; a measured ad campaign returned $219 in visitor spending per $1; record convention centre attendance; overnight visits spread evenly across the year (22 to 28% a quarter).
lessons_from_other_destinations.fit_for_calgary: Market the city as a destination in its own right, not only a road to the mountains; even seasonality is possible for a Rockies gateway.

sources.title: Denver tourism sets records in 2025 with 37.6M visitors

cautions: Tourism Calgary's visitor and spending figures are its own estimates (method in its reports); Statistics Canada's arrivals count where visitors enter Canada, not where they stay.
Seven million connecting travellers is Tourism Calgary's figure; the airport does not publish connecting traffic separately.
Lessons from other places depend on their own conditions (visa rules, hub airlines, climate, scale); say what would and would not carry over.
Growth has costs: crowding in Banff, housing pressure from short-term rentals; weigh them with the gains.

around_calgary.unesco: Alberta has six UNESCO World Heritage Sites, more than any other province; five are within about four and a half hours of Calgary: the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks (Banff, Yoho, Kootenay, Jasper), Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump, Dinosaur Provincial Park, Waterton Glacier International Peace Park and Writing-on-Stone/Áísínai'pi. The sixth, Wood Buffalo, is in the far north.

unesco_source.title: Alberta has the most UNESCO sites in Canada

kananaskis.plans: The province plans more campsites, trails and parking, a Highway 742 upgrade, and is exploring the All-Season Resorts Act for Kananaskis (its estimate: $2 billion a year in visitor spending); conservationists warn of crowding and wildlife impacts.

source.title: Province eyes big tourism growth in Kananaskis Country

banff_cannot_grow_beds.what: Banff's commercial space is capped by federal law (350,000 sq ft of new commercial floor area set in 1998, all allocated by 2013); a 175-room hotel at 600 Banff Avenue may be the last new hotel in Banff. With Banff's visitors at a record 4.5 million, new beds for Rockies visitors have to come from Canmore (itself limited) or Calgary.

source.title: Banff close to reaching commercial build-out

around_calgary.hub_argument: A visitor based in Calgary can reach mountains (Kananaskis in about an hour, Banff in under two), badlands and dinosaurs (Drumheller under two hours), Blackfoot history (Blackfoot Crossing, Head-Smashed-In) and Waterton, in day trips, with a city's hotel choice, prices, restaurants, events and airport. The study should test this: hotel supply and prices in Calgary against Banff and Canmore, the share of mountain visitors who sleep in Calgary, transport for visitors without a car (shuttles, tours, rail plans), and the risk of moving crowding rather than easing it.
